transcript.content: Hi, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Well, my regular doctor actually told me I needed to come see you. He says I've gotten too thin. 

I mean, I guess I can see what he's talking about. I clean buildings for a living, and I can definitely see my work pants just hanging loose on me lately. But... honestly, part of me still feels relieved when I step on the scale and the number is lower.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yes, I am. Honestly, if I eat something a bit heavier... like biscuits or pasta, I spend the rest of the day just scared it's going to show on me. I end up checking myself in the mirror, and I just keep thinking that I need to make up for what I ate somehow.
When you look at your body, do you feel fat even though other people say you are too thin?

I suppose I do. It’s just... when I stay small and neat, I feel like I'm handling everything right. But if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks the least bit full, I just feel like I've completely let myself go. So even if my doctor or anyone else tells me I'm too thin, that's just not what I see or feel in those moments.
Have you ever made yourself vomit after eating?
No, I haven't ever done that. I might feel really anxious after I eat, but... no, I don't make myself throw up.
Have you been deliberately eating much less in order to lose weight or avoid gaining weight?

Yes, I do. I cook regular plates for my husband and my mother-in-law, but... well, by the time I actually sit down at the table, I usually tell myself that just some coffee, a few vegetables, or maybe half a piece of toast is enough for me. It's just my way of making sure I don't put on weight.
What is your current weight?

Well, my regular doctor says I've gotten too thin. I don't know the exact number right this minute, but... I can definitely see my work pants hanging loose on me when I go in for my shift. But honestly, even knowing that, part of me still feels relieved when I step on the scale and see that the number is lower.
What is your height?
I'm not exactly sure, to be honest. I haven't had my height checked in a long time, so... I don't really know the exact number. Just average, I suppose.
Do you ever exercise specifically to burn off calories after eating?

No, I don't really do that. I mean, I'm on my feet most of the day for my job, cleaning and all, so I get plenty of movement in anyway. But... no, I don't do any extra exercises or work out specifically to burn off what I just ate.
Have your menstrual periods stopped?
Well, I'm 64, so... my periods stopped a long time ago. I went through menopause years back, so that's not really something that's happened recently.
Has your weight loss been intentional?

Well, no, not on purpose. I mean, I haven't been trying to lose weight, if that's what you're asking. I just... I haven't really noticed it all that much, to be honest. I guess with being on my feet all day at work and just keeping busy, it just sort of happens, but no, I'm not intentionally trying to drop any pounds.
Do you ever have times when you eat a large amount of food in a short period and feel unable to stop?

No, I don't really have anything like that. I don't eat large amounts of food all at once, and I never feel like I can't stop eating. I just eat my regular meals, whatever I can manage, and that's about it.
When you eat only coffee, vegetables, or half a piece of toast, are you doing that on purpose to keep from gaining weight?

Well... I suppose so, yes. If I eat something heavier, like biscuits or pasta, I just... I spend the rest of the day scared it's going to show on me. So I keep checking myself, you know, in the mirror or just feeling my waist, and thinking I need to make up for it somehow. So keeping it to just coffee or a bit of toast... it just feels safer.
Compared with your usual weight as an adult, are you much lighter now?

Yes, I am. My regular doctor actually told me recently that I've gotten too thin. And... well, I can see it myself, my work pants are hanging pretty loose on me these days. But if I'm being honest, even knowing that, part of me still feels relieved when I step on the scale and see that the number is lower.
